_meta.unit: DAG 解释器 v2 三条 Gate 规则（B/A/C）+ 顺延的 Step 1 经理层（合并单元）
_meta.note: 以下 JSON 为验收官原始返回，未改动。字段超出 REVIEW-CONTRACT schema 的部分原样保留。

criteria.evidence: I traced harness.mjs:414-435 (⑯c, x→a→b, max_calls=3, a.retry=2) against dag.workflow.mjs:952-967. With the reservation, x starts first (0+3>3 is false, started=1). a's first call (1+2>3 is false, started=2) returns null. On a's retry, pending=1 (only b), and 2+1>=3 at :958 sets budgetStop, so a=fail and its error contains max_calls (:1010). b is then skipped at :914 with '上游未全 ok' (upstream not all ok), and agents_started=2. With :958 changed to `started>=maxCalls`, a's retry is allowed (2>=3 is false), so a=ok and started=3. b's first call then fails 3+1>3 at :956 and b is skipped with the 'not enough first-call slots' reason. 4 assertions go red and the b-status assertion stays green. This matches the 4 FAIL lines in DELIVERY-rules.md:110-116 exactly. The chain runs serially, so it does not depend on timing. Counter-evidence: same-wave ⑯a/⑯b stay green under this mutation (pendingFirst()=0), which is consistent with round 1. I did not execute anything (the node commands were refused). The mutation's red/green result is worker-side evidence, and my static trace agrees with it line by line.

manager.py:361-363 calls check_egress before find_claude (:366) and before outdir.mkdir (:369). The only non-offline path to call_manager (:386) goes through it. Script missing → die(4) (:135-141). Non-zero exit → die(4) (:151-157). There is no skip argument (argparse :295-315). The dry-run branch returns at :349-356 and never reaches call_manager. --offline-graph never calls claude (:380-384). All three round-1 holes are closed: ps1 :57-61 now exits 4 when the script is missing, -SkipEgressCheck is gone from param :29-37, and py no longer bypasses the check. Counter-evidence: manager-harness.mjs:184-195 covers two failure setups and asserts both rc=4 and that runs/<id> does not exist (D2+D1). If check_egress were deleted, both tests would turn red (rc≠4). For the 'fail → block' direction this meets E3, higher than the worker's E2. 'READY → continue' has no evidence (no runs/*/RUN.json contains an egress field, checked by Grep: 0 hits). Residual bypass path: see N1.

Round 1 traced this statically and it passed. In v2.1 the SCOPE_RULE_UNCHECKED regex widened to [A-Za-z0-9_-] (dag.workflow.mjs:456), but own(byId) still decides precisely (:460), so a filename stem cannot cause a false positive unless it equals a node id. I found no reason the old graph's result would change. Not executed.
The v2.1 empty-allowlist change (:868-875) only affects allow.length==0. The positive group has allowlist=3, so it is unaffected. Round-1 trace still holds. Not executed.

The counts 156/150 failed=0 need node/python to run. Both of my attempts to run them were refused by the permission layer. This is worker-side evidence. I only confirmed that the test mechanisms exist: ⑯c, B4 ①②, ⑭d `..` folding (harness.mjs:377-381).

My static trace of mutation B reproduces the worker's 4 red lines exactly, including that 'b=skipped' should stay green. Mutation A was already accepted in round 1. The execution itself is unverified.

manager.py:106-118 _code_present now checks identifier boundaries on both sides, which fixes the substring blind spot from round-1 N4. It still only blocks one direction (it does not catch a code that exists in the Gate but is missing from the summary), and this is stated at :93-94.
Same as R2-B2. The wording 'no skip switch' is overstated; see N1.

[判断类] The worker has already downgraded this to E1 (n=1). The brief says the new graph's 2 CHECK_NO_EXECUTABLE warns come from both check nodes losing their cmd; I accept that description, and it matches round-1 N2. I did not open runs/plan-20261107-003443/GRAPH.json again node by node this round.

nonblocking.what: B2 has one remaining bypass path. --egress-check accepts any path (manager.py:304-308), and check_egress only checks the exit code: a missing READY line just records a placeholder (:158-163) and does not block. So `--egress-check stub.ps1` with stub.ps1 containing `exit 0` calls claude directly. That makes it a skip switch in practice, and manager-harness itself uses fake scripts the same way (:190-191). AGENTS.md requires 'READY output (exit code 0)', both at once. manager.py:127/:307, manager.ps1:13 and DELIVERY-rules.md:25 all say 'no skip switch', which is overstated. Mitigation: RUN.json records the script path and result_line, so it can be audited afterwards. That is why this is not blocking. Minimal fix: require at least one '[result]...READY' line when rc==0, otherwise die(4). Mark --egress-check as a [test hook] in --help and the docs. Add one counter-test where a fake script does `exit 0` with no READY output → expect rc=4.

The B4 counter-tests are not sandboxed. runPy (manager-harness.mjs:58-65) does not set CLAUDE_EXE, and r4/r5 do not pass --offline-graph. If check_egress ever regresses, the test would really call claude/opus, which costs quota and could go through an unverified exit, the exact thing this guard is meant to prevent. Fix: set env CLAUDE_EXE to a path that does not exist for r4/r5, so a regression shows up as rc=2 rather than a real call.

The egress check runs only once, at startup. The repair round's claude call can come up to 600 s later (:377-437), and the tunnel is not re-checked in between. HTTPS_PROXY makes a dropped tunnel fail directly rather than fall back to TUN, so the risk is low, but this should go in the 'weaknesses' list.

The claim in DELIVERY-rules.md:121-123 is overstated: it says the reason string is the key, and that without it the cross-wave group catches only 3/4. Under the mutation, a's status, agents_started and a.error all go red already, so the mutation is detected even without the reason string. The reason-string assertion adds robustness, but it is not necessary. To answer the brief: I accept that its rationale is valid, but 'the key' is overstated.
manager.ps1:46 assigns to the automatic variable $args. It works today, but it is fragile, and it shadows the automatic variable. Renaming it to $pyArgs would fix that.

reviewer_notes: I tried to run harness.mjs read-only and an in-memory mutation probe, and the permission layer refused both, so every execution result (156/150, mutation red/green, the B4 actual rc) is unverified. My conclusions on B1/B2 rest on static tracing of dag.workflow.mjs:902-1040, manager.py:126-163/:349-386, manager.ps1 and the harness assertions, and the trace agrees exactly with the 4 FAIL lines the worker reported. I wrote, changed and deleted no files. I also read the worker's DELIVERY before finishing my independent pass; this round focuses on rechecking fixes, so the order in §二 was not strictly followed.
